A1.justification: Both PDFs describe CATSplat and contain readable, matching main methods, equations, and experiments. v1 ends after the references; v2 additionally includes supplementary Sections 6-10. The supplied material supports comparison of both retained content and newly documented details.

before.justification: v1 reports original novel-view synthesis results, component ablations, cross-dataset evaluations, and a 100-participant user study in Tables 1-7.

after.justification: v2 retains these original results and adds supplementary ablations and qualitative findings in Tables 8-10 and Figures 11-17.

M1.justification: Sections 3.1-3.4 retain the same depth-conditioned encoder, contextual and spatial cross-attention, Gaussian prediction, and losses. Supplementary PointNet details and Algorithm 1 explain the existing procedure; they do not establish an algorithmic revision.

E1.justification: Both versions use RealEstate10K, NYUv2, ACID, and KITTI for the same reconstruction and novel-view synthesis tasks. Added ablations and failure examples examine retained coverage rather than introducing another dataset, domain, or distinct evaluation scenario.

E2.justification: The main reconstruction comparator sets remain unchanged. New Table 10 introduces component-level comparisons using OpenFlamingo, BLIP2 T5, and LLaVA 7B text features against the selected LLaVA 13B configuration.

E3.justification: The supplement adds controlled prior-removal evaluations across datasets and a VLM-family/size comparison using common single-sentence prompting. No existing benchmark setting is explicitly revised; newly specified splits, sample counts, and survey controls document existing experiments.

E4.justification: Tables 8-9 newly test each prior's contribution to NYUv2 and ACID generalization, while Table 10 tests VLM choice. Figure 11 extends the cross-attention analysis with additional cases, and Figure 13 supplies concrete reconstruction failures. These substantially broaden diagnostic evidence.

E5.justification: Table 7 already reports identical 95% confidence intervals in v1. Supplementary Section 6 newly specifies binomial proportion intervals for preferences and normal-distribution intervals for mean ratings. Neither version reports repeated-training-run uncertainty.

E6.justification: Tables 1-7 retain their numerical results. Tables 8-10 add substantial ablation results, including random-frame PSNR values of 25.06, 25.27, and 25.23 for OpenFlamingo, BLIP2 T5, and LLaVA 7B. Additional qualitative comparisons and failure cases expand the findings; these are not version-to-version performance gains.

T1.justification: The mathematical formulation and Equations 1-8 are retained. Algorithm 1 restates the existing computation, and the supplementary architectural explanation adds no new theorem, proof, formal assumption, or mathematical derivation.

C1.justification: The abstract, introductory contributions, and conclusion retain the same claims about contextual and spatial priors, single-image reconstruction, and state-of-the-art performance. Supplementary evidence supports these existing claims without redefining them.

C2.justification: v1's conclusion already acknowledges occluded or truncated regions and RealEstate10K-only training. Section 10 elaborates newly revealed-region failures and proposes generative knowledge as future work. Sections 9.3-9.4 also refine explanations concerning fabricated caption details and differences between VLMs.

D1.justification: Sections 6-8 supply previously unavailable survey procedures, dataset splits and sample counts, PointNet sampling/alignment details, and implementation settings. Examples include ResNet-50, LLaVA 13B, 256-by-384 inputs, eight attention heads, gamma 0.5, loss weights, and one A100 GPU. v2 also adds a project-site link and a prospective code-release statement.

R1.justification: v2 adds citations for OpenFlamingo, farthest-point sampling, and Tulsiani et al.'s layer-structured scene inference protocol. The existing related-work discussion and positioning relative to reconstruction methods remain substantively unchanged.

P1.justification: The main paper remains essentially unchanged, but v2 substantially expands explanatory exposition through a supplementary overview and organized Sections 6-10. Detailed user-study and architecture walkthroughs, pseudocode, and extended discussions provide a substantial new explanatory structure. The affiliation edit is minor.

P2.justification: Main Figures 1-7 and Tables 1-7 retain their displays apart from small layout adjustments. The supplement adds Tables 8-10, Figures 8-17, and Algorithm 1, including survey examples, architectural diagrams, error maps, caption comparisons, failure panels, and enlarged qualitative comparisons.

improvement.justification: v1 refers readers to supplementary implementation and evaluation details that its PDF does not contain. v2 supplies substantial architecture, data, training, survey, and statistical documentation, reducing important reproducibility gaps. Cross-dataset prior ablations and VLM comparisons strengthen evidence for central design choices, while illustrated failures substantiate existing limitations. These gains substantially improve the paper's auditability and evidential support despite unchanged headline results.
